metadata.title: Epic 256 reconciled atomic decision ledger
metadata.note: Historical frequency is evidence, not authority. This ledger contains no synthesis or future values ratification.

integrity_expression.rationale: Twenty-three open choices could plausibly prefer practical legibility, permissive authoring, compatibility aliases, or graceful use over tighter semantic constraints. The remaining unresolved cards either do not put this axis in tension, would codify explicit meaning whichever alternative wins, or are manifestations that would not independently become eligible precedent votes. Even if every listed card resolved toward Expression, Integrity retains 70.16% of the worst-case eligible pool.

continuity_evolution.rationale: There is no threshold bias to protect: Evolution is a 51-to-33 plurality, not a 70% primary bias. The listed open dispositions can plausibly retain aliases, properties, permissive shapes, historical boundaries, current readers, or current tooling, and collectively could reverse that plurality. This axis therefore remains historically mixed regardless of the worst-case calculation.

coherence_autonomy.rationale: Thirteen open choices could plausibly prefer layer-specific enforcement, local identifier freedom, open properties, bounded extension ownership, or implementation autonomy. Repeated per-entity tag questions are treated as manifestations of the one unresolved tags-policy precedent rather than independent constitutional votes. Even if every listed card resolved toward Autonomy, Coherence retains 70.18% of the worst-case eligible pool and all eight currently counted family majorities.

decisions.title: Replace valueType with orthogonal fieldType facets
decisions.decision_statement: A Field expresses datatype, cardinality, value domain, format, and constraints as independent fieldType facets instead of extending the conflated valueType enum with more parallel patch properties.

sources.excerpt: Accepted RFC-032 Change A replaces valueType with the decomposed fieldType model; its rationale records the rejected ninth-value alternative.
The effective Field schema requires fieldType and defines its orthogonal facets.

alternatives: Keep valueType and add composite as a ninth enum value.
Keep separate contentFormat, allowed-values, validation-rule, and repeatable mechanisms.
decisions.accepted_cost: All Field definitions required a breaking, scripted definition-layer migration and existing readers temporarily could not load them.
supersedes: Field.valueType and its parallel patch-property model

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Keeping convenient legacy encodings would preserve ambiguity between independent semantic facets.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: Presentation concerns remain available outside fieldType.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: The semantic model becomes harder to author than the ambiguity it removes.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Preserving the public legacy shape would freeze a model unable to describe itself.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: The migration was deterministic, idempotent, corpus-wide, and instance cutover was separately gated.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Breaking changes land without complete migration and compatibility evidence.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Parallel mechanisms would permit incompatible descriptions of the same concern.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Package-managed vocabularies and open maps preserve bounded extension points.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: One core type vocabulary crowds out legitimate domain-owned meaning.

decisions.coding_notes: Atomic choice is replacement of the type-description mechanism; individual new datatype constructs are separate cards. Matches calibrated precedent E256-A90 without reusing its research ID.

alternatives: Keep anonymous FieldGroup-only range identity.

sources.excerpt: The accepted rationale says editorHint and compositeRenderer map to no semantic axis and are consolidated by the rendering follow-up instead of fieldType.

decisions.title: Express the definition-layer metamodel in its own Field and Type language
decisions.decision_statement: Field, Type, FieldAssignment, and the in-scope value objects are authored as SRS definitions in the canonical com.semanticops.srs/metamodel package, replacing RFC-004's parallel schema-source vocabulary.

sources.excerpt: Accepted RFC-033 defines the ten-Type self-hosted metamodel package and [R7] supersedes RFC-004's parallel vocabulary.
The current canonical metamodel package contains the generated Field and Type definitions.

alternatives: Keep RFC-004 schema-definition/schema-member as a second source language.
Define the metamodel only through hand-authored JSON Schema.
decisions.accepted_cost: The system must bootstrap a language expressed in itself and maintain closure evidence for a recursive package.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: A parallel schema-source language would create two authorities for the same semantic definitions.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: Generated JSON Schema remains the interoperable runtime expression.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Self-description is maintained ceremonially while runtime meaning diverges from it.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Retaining RFC-004's vocabulary would preserve historical work but perpetuate the duplicate source.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: Its reusable projection rules are retained rather than discarded.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Consolidation deletes reusable historical contracts along with obsolete source artifacts.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Multiple schema vocabularies would let model meaning fork across toolchains.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Domain packages still author Types and Fields within the same shared language.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: The core metamodel claims concerns that belong to independent extension packages.

decisions.coding_notes: Scope is the definition layer; the RFC explicitly defers instance-layer Record/Relation/Container self-hosting.

decisions.title: Resolve the metamodel through ordinary packageRefs rather than implicit merge
decisions.decision_statement: The metamodel package is an explicit ordinary packageRef-resolved package; foundational status reserves its specific identities but does not make com.semanticops.srs implicitly available or reserve the entire namespace.

sources.excerpt: RFC-033 Rev 2 rejects its earlier always-implicit proposal, preserving RFC-029 packageRef resolution and reserving only specific metamodel identities.
The effective repository manifest resolves the metamodel by packageRef.

alternatives: Implicitly merge every com.semanticops.srs metamodel type into all repositories.
Reserve the entire namespace against package ownership.
decisions.accepted_cost: Repositories and tools that need metamodel records must resolve an explicit dependency even though the runtime seed is foundational.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Implicit availability would blur the distinct roles of runtime bootstrap schema and toolchain-consumed metamodel records.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: The frozen seed is still always available to load records.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Layer purity forces users to configure dependencies that have no meaningful choice.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Implicit merge would break the existing package resolution contract established by RFC-029.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: A new metamodel package is still added through the established extension mechanism.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Legacy resolution rules block a demonstrably simpler bootstrap design.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: A namespace-wide implicit package would impose a hidden global dependency and reservation on every repository.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Specific canonical metamodel IDs and shared package resolution rules preserve coherence.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: Explicit ownership permits repositories to substitute incompatible foundational definitions.

decisions.coding_notes: Preserves the original decision and explicit supersession of RFC-033 Rev 1 rather than rewriting the history.

decisions.title: Retain committed Field and Type schemas as the runtime bootstrap fixed point
decisions.decision_statement: The loader consumes committed field.json and type.json as-is and never derives them from the metamodel records at runtime, even after records become the build-time authorship source.

sources.excerpt: Accepted RFC-033 [R3] makes the two schemas the bootstrap fixed point and forbids runtime re-derivation.
The effective schema is marked as the frozen seed loaded as committed.

alternatives: Re-derive the schema at process startup from records that themselves require the schema to parse.
Avoid self-hosted records and retain hand-authored schemas as the only representation.
decisions.accepted_cost: The project retains a bootstrap artifact in addition to the self-hosted records and must check them for drift at build time.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Runtime generation would require trusting records before their defining schema is available.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: Self-hosted records remain inspectable and become the planned build-time authorship source.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: The bootstrap artifact becomes a second hand-edited semantic authority.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Removing the independent base case would make existing loaders unable to parse the definition of their own model.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: The later authorship flip can regenerate the committed fixed point once closure is proven.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Bootstrap caution blocks the build-time source flip after all preconditions pass.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Implementations could invent different bootstrap derivations.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: The fixed artifact is portable and does not require a particular generator at runtime.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: One committed artifact prevents independently conforming implementations.

decisions.coding_notes: Matches calibrated precedent E256-A91. The later authorship direction is not equivalent to runtime derivation.

decisions.title: Make projection loss explicit in a per-emitter fidelity contract
decisions.decision_statement: Every metamodel feature is classified as authoritative or approximated for each emitter; authoritative meaning cannot be silently dropped and approximated meaning must emit its documented lossy shape.

sources.excerpt: Accepted RFC-033 [R5] requires a per-emitter authoritative/approximated classification and forbids silent omission.
The current dashboard records fidelity and coverage separately for the JSON Schema emitter.

alternatives: Describe generation as lossless despite known semantic gaps.
Silently omit constructs that a target cannot represent.
decisions.accepted_cost: Each emitter maintains an explicit feature matrix, lossy-shape contract, and tests rather than claiming simple universal equivalence.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: A convenient target projection could silently erase semantics while still appearing valid.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: Approximated output remains usable and is emitted in a documented form rather than prohibited.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Fidelity bookkeeping grows while no consumer depends on the distinctions.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: The cited evidence does not place the two poles of this axis in tension for this atomic decision.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: No counter-pole safeguard is inferred because this axis is not expressed by the evidence.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Do not manufacture an axis direction from source vocabulary alone.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Each emitter could choose undisclosed losses and produce artifacts with incomparable meaning.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Targets may use different approximations as long as each is explicit and tested.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: A common matrix prevents target-native representations that preserve more meaning.

decisions.coding_notes: Fidelity and metamodel coverage are explicitly separate; this card concerns fidelity only. Audit removed an unsupported temporal direction.

decisions.title: Gate data-model compatibility with a monotonic revision stamp
decisions.decision_statement: Manifests and generated bundles carry a monotonic non-negative dataModelRevision, with absence treated as revision 0 and the valueType-to-fieldType migration registered and stamped as revision 1.

sources.excerpt: Accepted RFC-033 [R6] defines the integer generation stamp, absent-as-zero behavior, migration 1, and bundle propagation.
The effective repository manifest is stamped dataModelRevision 1.

alternatives: Use a 2.0.x semver-looking model version.
Use shape detection alone without a coarse compatibility gate.
Reject unstamped revision-0 repositories.
decisions.accepted_cost: The project maintains a separate coarse generation counter alongside artifact versions and must propagate it through migrations and bundles.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: A semver-looking patch could falsely imply backward compatibility for a breaking data-model shape.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: The integer is deliberately coarse; shape detection remains the precise mechanism.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: The stamp is mistaken for complete semantic compatibility proof.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Strictly requiring the new stamp would make legacy repositories unable to reach the migration; no gate would make newer repositories unsafe to load.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: Absent means 0 for reachability, while newer-than-binary revisions fail closed.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Legacy defaulting conceals a repository whose actual shape disagrees with revision 0.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Repositories, generated bundles, and runtimes could disagree about the data-model generation.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: The gate makes no claim about package versioning or domain-owned evolution.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: A global revision blocks independently compatible package changes.

decisions.coding_notes: Balanced continuity/evolution is intentional and therefore off-cube for that axis.

decisions.title: Replace impossible seed byte-equality with two strict, honest verification tiers
decisions.decision_statement: Emitter determinism is checked byte-for-byte against its own goldens, while semantic closure against the hand-authored seed is an explicit normalized emitter-subset relation with exclusions and registered divergences.

sources.excerpt: Accepted RFC-035 refines RFC-033 R4(b): byte parity is against emitter goldens and seed closure uses reference resolution, explicit exclusions, and a divergence register.
The delivered closure test enforces the authoritative subset and reports exclusions and divergence.

alternatives: Require literal equality with a seed whose intentional structure cannot be regenerated.
Loosen or doctor the emitter and seed until a single superficial diff passes.
Use only a deterministic golden without semantic closure.
decisions.accepted_cost: Verification has two distinct gates plus an exclusion and divergence register that reviewers must maintain.
supersedes: RFC-033 R4(b) literal byte-for-byte seed wording

integrity_expression.counterfactual: A cosmetically simple equality claim would be false or would force semantic and structural distortions.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: Byte-for-byte reproducibility remains strict where it is meaningful, against emitter-owned goldens.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Normalization and exclusions become loopholes that hide real drift.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Preserving accepted wording literally would make a correct emitter impossible to certify.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: The earlier intent is explicitly preserved and the supersession is documented rather than silently rewritten.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Accepted obligations are weakened whenever implementation becomes inconvenient.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Different implementations could claim closure using undocumented normalizations.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Emitter-owned keys and target syntax remain locally selectable within the published comparison contract.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: One verification normalization masks target-specific correctness failures.

decisions.coding_notes: Original RFC-033 wording and RFC-035 supersession are both preserved in sources.

decisions.title: Bind Rust projection to the accepted fieldType and emitter contracts
decisions.decision_statement: The Rust implementation adopts the RFC-032 fieldType model and implements the RFC-035 projection through core, CLI, and WASM surfaces with byte-parity against the reference emitter rather than maintaining its earlier independent mapping.

sources.excerpt: Merged PR #778 reports fieldType adoption, reference-emitter byte parity for entity schemas and bundle, and CLI/WASM bindings.
RFC-035 makes the Rust service a binding of the sanctioned emitter rather than an independent projection.

alternatives: Keep the pre-RFC-032 Rust mapping as an independent source of projection semantics.
Leave the accepted model Node-only.
decisions.accepted_cost: Rust consumers underwent a breaking model migration and serialization ordering became part of cross-language parity.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: An independent mapping could produce usable schemas with meaning that diverged from the accepted projection.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: The implementation exposes practical CLI and WASM surfaces and reports inexpressible constraints.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Byte parity is treated as sufficient even when two implementations share the same semantic defect.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Retaining the embedded legacy model would keep existing code stable but leave the binary unable to load the epic's records.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: Revision-0 repositories load and can migrate; regression tests cover earlier behavior.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Implementation migration breaks consumers beyond the accepted model boundary.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Rust could become a second standards authority with its own mapping.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Rust chooses internal types and serialization machinery while matching the public contract.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: Reference parity prevents a conforming implementation from choosing a better internal design.

decisions.coding_notes: Documented as a delivered consequence, not an additional bias vote; PR #778 also contains independent unknown-field and aiGuidance decisions assigned to other research families.

decisions.title: Make the authoritative store, not the manifest, define repository content
decisions.decision_statement: A repository's authoritative content is what its authoritative store reports across the instance, relation, container, source-document, definition, and extension sets; manifest.json is not content authority except for its inline root container.

sources.excerpt: Accepted RFC-038 Change A names six authoritative sets and assigns authority to the backing store rather than an index file.
Rule R1 makes the store authoritative and reserves only the inline root-container exception for the manifest.

alternatives: Keep manifest indexes authoritative.
Let each implementation choose between index and tree authority.
decisions.accepted_cost: Implementations must replace index-driven enumeration and accept a coordinated breaking storage migration.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: A stale or implementation-selected index could hide objects that the repository actually stores.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: The manifest remains the stable entry point and descriptor.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Store discovery becomes so implicit that authors cannot explain why an object is or is not content.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Preserving index authority would retain a ratified contradiction and the known parallel-writer conflict.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: The inline root-container authority and logical identities are preserved.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Authority changes without an identity-complete migration or generation gate.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Filesystem, JSON, memory, and database implementations could expose different membership semantics.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Each backend decides how its authoritative store answers the common logical query.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: A common contract forces every backend to emulate filesystem paths or a manifest index.

decisions.coding_notes: This card records the authority choice only; discovery, diagnostics, and migration gates are separate decisions.

decisions.title: Retain one stable manifest as descriptor while removing live inventories
decisions.decision_statement: Every repository retains exactly one manifest.json for identity and stable configuration, including the canonical inline root container, while generation-2 manifests forbid the five live inventory or cache properties and routine unscoped writes do not touch the manifest.

sources.excerpt: Change A retains the manifest as required descriptor and removes its role as a content inventory.
Rule R2 forbids instanceIndex, containerIndex, sourceDocumentIndex, relationsChecksums, and relationsPath at revision 2.

alternatives: Remove the manifest entirely.
Retain the inventories as maintained caches.
Move routine membership writes into the root container.
decisions.accepted_cost: The manifest's updatedAt no longer tracks routine repository activity and inventory consumers must move to catalog enumeration.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: A convenient singleton cache would remain a competing statement of repository meaning.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: Identity and configuration stay easy to locate in one stable entry point.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Removing projections also removes useful deliberate configuration or orientation.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Eliminating the descriptor or relocating root-container authority would create unrelated identity and composition changes.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: The obsolete inventory contract is removed rather than indefinitely deprecated.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Stable descriptor status is used to retain frequently mutated derived state.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Repositories could expose different entry points and root-container authority rules.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Only deliberate configuration and membership edits share the descriptor; ordinary writes remain isolated.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: The common descriptor grows into a central registry for independent semantic objects.

decisions.coding_notes: The retained descriptor and removal of inventory authority are one contrasted role decision; root composition semantics remain outside RFC-038.

decisions.title: Discover fixed reserved roots by conforming package presence
decisions.decision_statement: Filesystem discovery recursively scans fixed records, notes, and typed-records roots at the repository root and every conforming local-package root discovered by package.json presence, never by packageRefs or another configured path list.

sources.excerpt: Change B rejects declared-package discovery after measuring seven instances under an undeclared but conforming local package root.
Rules R3 and R4 define presence-keyed roots and diagnose SRS-shaped near-miss package manifests without treating npm manifests as errors.

alternatives: Scan the whole repository by shape.
Configure roots in the manifest.
Limit package discovery to packageRefs.
decisions.accepted_cost: The loader must search for package anchors and diagnose malformed SRS package manifests rather than reading one configured list.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Configured roots already omit seven live instances and hide the definitions needed to detect a live dangling fieldId.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: The root vocabulary is small, fixed, and implementation-defined subfolders remain legal.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Discovery expands beyond intentional boundaries and turns incidental files into semantic members.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Keeping configured enumeration would preserve an incomplete legacy model.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: Legacy top-level roots and existing recursive subfolders remain recognized.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: New roots invalidate conforming legacy content without measured necessity.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Locally configured root lists could give identical trees different membership.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Packages may live anywhere in the repository subtree and organize their root contents freely.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: The fixed root set prevents a legitimate package-owned storage pattern from being represented.

decisions.coding_notes: Near-miss package diagnostics are a safeguard of the same discovery choice, not an extra constitutional vote.

decisions.title: Apply a closed policy only inside explicit repository locations
decisions.decision_statement: Candidate files inside reserved repository locations must be recognized SRS entities, recognized sidecars, or diagnosed errors, while content outside those locations and permitted opaque payloads are application content that repository operations neither interpret nor modify.

sources.excerpt: Change D defines reserved locations, most-specific classification, a closed candidate policy, and opaque source payload protection.
Rules R9 and R10 forbid silent skipping inside the boundary and forbid semantic interpretation outside it.

alternatives: Scan all repository files by shape.
Silently ignore malformed or unknown files under reserved locations.
Treat every JSON file under a reserved root as an instance.
decisions.accepted_cost: Reserved locations become strict and a single malformed candidate can block loading; authors must place non-member SRS-shaped material outside them.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Silent skips inside an authoritative boundary make an incomplete repository look successful.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: Opaque source payloads are exempted from SRS classification and preserved.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Strictness expands to files that make no semantic claim.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: The choice sets a boundary rather than choosing migration or compatibility.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: Existing application content outside reserved locations remains untouched.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Previously tolerated malformed candidates surface without actionable diagnostics.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Whole-tree discovery would let the SRS contract appropriate application-owned files merely because their shape matches.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Inside explicitly shared locations all implementations apply the same closed candidate rules.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: Local-content protection becomes a loophole for hiding semantic claims just outside the boundary.

decisions.coding_notes: This is the boundary decision; entity classification and fatality are coded separately.

decisions.title: Classify objects by validated content rather than location or declaration alone
decisions.decision_statement: Object kind and tier come from validated content: a declared schema must validate and resolve to exactly one admissible entity without shape fallback, while an object without a schema must validate as exactly one admissible entity; path never determines kind or tier.

sources.excerpt: Change C adopts declared-then-validated classification with exact-shape fallback only when schema is absent.
Rules R6 through R8 make content authoritative for classification and preserve unlabelled objects only through exact validation.

alternatives: Infer tier from folder names.
Trust any declared $schema without validation.
Require $schema on every object.
Always fall back to shape after a bad declaration.
decisions.accepted_cost: Loaders need full schema resolution and exact admissible-set validation, including pairwise distinguishability checks.

coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: A closed core entity set prevents legitimate domain composition.

decisions.coding_notes: The schema-present and schema-absent branches form one conditional classifier contract and cannot be split without losing the explicit fallback boundary.

coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Packages still choose which supported definition kinds and definitions they declare.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: Completeness is confused with requiring every package to implement every kind.

decisions.coding_notes: Narrowed to kind-source authority; closed schema completeness is D20.

decisions.title: Reject duplicate logical identifiers without precedence
decisions.decision_statement: Two objects in one authoritative set that claim the same logical identifier are an error naming every conflicting locator; implementations may not choose a winner by path, recency, or enumeration order.

sources.excerpt: Presence discovery exposes 27 duplicate definition IDs in muSrs and the RFC refuses silent coalescing even for byte-identical copies.
Rule R12 requires all-locator duplicate diagnostics and forbids conflict resolution by precedence, recency, or enumeration order.

alternatives: Let first-discovered or newest object win.
Coalesce byte-identical objects.
Scope uniqueness only to paths or packages.

integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: Diagnostics name every locator so the conflict is practical to repair.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Global uniqueness rejects intentionally scoped identities whose schema defines a narrower domain.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Preserving hidden duplicates would make the new complete catalog ambiguous.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: Logical IDs remain unchanged; only conflicting duplicate ownership is repaired.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Repairs discard provenance or history merely because two current files collide.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Packages or adapters could claim incompatible local winners for one shared logical identity.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Extension uniqueness remains keyed by its schema-defined kind and ID rather than one global namespace.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: The uniqueness domain expands beyond the authoritative set defined by the entity contract.

decisions.title: Require every reference to resolve to exactly one target
decisions.decision_statement: Every semantic reference resolves to exactly one object in its named authoritative set; zero or multiple targets are errors identifying the referring object, property, identifier, and conflicting locators, making the live #307 dangling fieldId a cutover prerequisite rather than a warning.

Rule R13 requires exact-one resolution and names the target set for field assignments, relations, containers, and source references.

alternatives: Warn and continue on dangling references.
Resolve against one undifferentiated repository set.
Accept multiple targets and choose by precedence.
decisions.accepted_cost: Existing hidden defects become fatal prerequisites and loaders must retain enough locator context for complete diagnostics.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Continuing with a missing or ambiguous target would fabricate or omit semantic relationships.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: Errors identify the referring property and all known locators to support repair.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Every soft, external, or intentionally deferred link is treated as a closed-world reference.

continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: The intended existing Field identity is repaired rather than replaced wholesale.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Validation breaks old repositories without an explicit migration path and reference parity check.

coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: The target set is property-specific rather than one centrally flattened object namespace.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: Exact-one rules are applied where an extension explicitly defines open or federated resolution.

decisions.decision_statement: Any error under a reserved repository location is fatal to repository loading; an implementation cannot report a partial catalog as successfully loaded.

Rule R24 makes reserved-location errors fatal to load while requiring validation to collect all diagnostics.

alternatives: Load every valid object and warn about omitted invalid candidates.
Make only instance-file errors fatal.

integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: Validation accumulates all errors and stable identifiers make failures diagnosable.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: A non-semantic presentation or optional extension failure blocks access to otherwise valid meaning.

coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Diagnostics can remain implementation-specific in presentation while carrying stable IDs and severity.

decisions.decision_statement: At generation 2 each Relation is stored as one independent live relations/<relationId>.json object, and changing it does not read or write another Relation file.

sources.excerpt: Change E selects one relation per file, rejects collection retention in snapshots, and keeps identity in file rather than deriving it from filename.
Rule R11 makes relation writes independent and forbids live generation-2 collection files.

decisions.accepted_cost: The corpus must split relation collections into many independently written files.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: A semantic filename or folder would create a second competing classification beside relationId and relationType.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: The UUID locator is deterministic and a filename mismatch yields an actionable error.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Identity purity makes repository browsing needlessly opaque without derived views.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Retaining collections in any generation-2 surface would preserve shared-write contention and two loader paths.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: Every relation field and logical ID is preserved through deterministic conversion.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: A breaking storage rewrite proceeds without relation-count and endpoint parity.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Independent writers would continue coordinating through one collection file or shard.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: All relation objects share one closed wire schema, flat location, and total ordering rule.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: Write isolation fragments operations that require atomic semantic coordination.

integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Compatibility is declined without rechecking whether external users now exist.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: An old reader or upgrade window would preserve runtime continuity with generation 1.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: The complete named first-party corpus migrates together and git history preserves the old state.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: A zero window is reused after the project has acquired external compatibility obligations.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: A compatibility period would allow different first-party components to remain on different generations.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Explicit opt-in migration tooling remains the one component allowed to interpret old data.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: Uniform generation is valued more than legitimate independent consumer schedules.

decisions.coding_notes: The no-window choice is split from rollback because either policy could be changed independently.

decisions.title: Use git history as cutover rollback
decisions.decision_statement: Rollback is a git revert of the complete cutover train, returning code and first-party data together; no downgrade converter is provided.

sources.excerpt: Accepted RFC-039 defines rollback as git revert of the train, with git history as recovery and no downgrade converter.
The cutover tracker requires baselines, before/after identity sets, hashes, and validation evidence for each migration target.

alternatives: Build and maintain a generation-2 to generation-1 downgrade converter.
Roll back code while leaving migrated data in place.
Treat the migration as irreversible.
decisions.accepted_cost: Rollback reverts the entire coordinated train and cannot selectively preserve later generation-2 edits.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: A downgrade transform could approximate or discard semantics that generation 1 cannot represent.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: A simple repository-native revert remains practical for the bounded first-party corpus.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Exact historical recovery is unavailable because required external state was never captured.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Without a recovery path, a failed breaking cutover could not restore the last coherent code-and-data state.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: Rollback does not require preserving the old format in current runtime code.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Recovery through history is invoked where users need forward migration of post-cutover work.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: The selected evidence does not compare shared and local ownership for rollback.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: No coherence claim is inferred.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: Different repositories cannot return to a mutually compatible baseline.

decisions.coding_notes: Recovery policy, not a vote for every mechanical file reversion.

decisions.title: Migrate every named first-party artifact to the final contract
decisions.decision_statement: The cutover includes the SRS specification repository, muSrs, maintained packages, fixtures, examples, seeds, snapshots, and schema mirrors; no known first-party target is deferred as a compatibility population.

sources.excerpt: The epic's First-party corpus boundary requires every named first-party repository and artifact to reach the final combined contract directly.
Accepted RFC-038 fixes the migration corpus and rejects an unmentioned or deferred repository population.

alternatives: Migrate only the main srs repository.
Leave packages and snapshots on their historical generations.
Treat clients and schema mirrors as post-cutover follow-ons.
decisions.accepted_cost: The gate expands across multiple repositories and artifact forms, increasing coordination and validation work before either design can ship.
supersedes: Repository-scoped migration inventories that omitted muSrs, fixtures, mirrors, or packages

integrity_expression.counterfactual: An omitted first-party artifact would remain a contradictory, misleading expression of the project contract.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: The boundary is finite and enumerated rather than claiming unknown external populations.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: The inventory absorbs abandoned or purely historical artifacts with no effective role.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Deferring known artifacts would preserve old generations alongside the final contract.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: Migration preserves logical IDs, semantic content, relations, containers, source documents, and valid history.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Forced migration rewrites artifacts whose immutable historical form is itself meaningful.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Independent first-party schedules would leave clients and corpora on incompatible authority and carrier contracts.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Each repository retains a named owning issue and validates through its own implementation boundary.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: A shared release gate makes unrelated repositories unable to progress independently.

decisions.coding_notes: This boundary decision does not count individual migrated files or repositories as additional decisions.

decisions.title: Migrate fixture packages without inventing repository identity
decisions.decision_statement: First-party fixture packages are migrated and stamped to the final package contract, while fixture trees remain test inputs: they receive no repository marker or generation-2 repository identity and their relation collections are not migrated.

sources.excerpt: The owner explicitly distinguishes fixture packages, which reach the contract, from fixture repositories, which remain test data without invented identity.
Accepted RFC-038 excludes the discovery and RFC-032 fixture trees from repository migration while retaining them as test inputs.
The reconciliation records the direct owner boundary: stamp the package, do not turn its containing fixture tree into a repository.

alternatives: Exclude fixture packages from the final contract.
Turn every fixture tree into a generation-2 repository to simplify migration arithmetic.
decisions.accepted_cost: Migration code and inventories must distinguish package conformance from repository identity instead of treating the containing directory as one homogeneous unit.
supersedes: RFC-038 stamping inventory that omitted the thirteenth fixture package

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Inventing repository identity would misstate what the test tree is, while leaving its package stale would misstate the package contract.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: The fixture remains usable as test input and its package description is rewritten in current fieldType terms.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Strict identity distinctions make fixtures difficult to load or exercise.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Leaving the fixture package at generation 0 would preserve a removed field model that final readers reject.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: Scenario and instance IDs, values, order, and legacy expected results are preserved.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Fixture migration silently changes the oracle it is supposed to preserve.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: A uniform rule that every package-bearing tree is a repository would impose identity the fixture does not claim.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: The package inside the fixture still conforms to the same shared generation-2 package contract.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: Local classification becomes a loophole for stale or unreadable packages.

decisions.coding_notes: Potential counter-pole case for synthesis; exception classification is deferred until a family-spanning bias exists. Reclassified as the migration manifestation of D15 to prevent a second conceptual vote.

decisions.title: Migrate published governance packages in place
decisions.decision_statement: Both published com.mudemocracy.governance package versions migrate in place with their consumers rather than remaining frozen at generation 0 or waiting for a newly published version.

sources.excerpt: Accepted RFC-038 brings both published governance packages into the cutover because generation-2 readers otherwise reject them, superseding RFC-039's earlier #286 scheduling note.
The post-acceptance reconciliation states that freeze is no longer available and both versions migrate in place within #297.

alternatives: Freeze the two released versions exactly as published.
Publish only a new migrated version and leave old versions readable through compatibility support.
decisions.accepted_cost: Artifacts labelled as already published versions are rewritten, so byte-level immutability yields to a generation-wide semantic cutover.
supersedes: RFC-039 and #286 deferral of published governance package disposition

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Frozen packages would retain a representation the final reader rejects and cease to express usable package meaning.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: Logical package versions, IDs, and semantic content are preserved through the in-place transform.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Semantic usability becomes a license to rewrite historical artifacts without a traceable baseline.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Freezing published bytes would preserve artifact continuity at the expense of final-generation readability.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: Before/after hashes and logical identity sets record what changed, and git preserves original bytes.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: A published-version immutability promise actually relied on by consumers is overridden.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Published packages would occupy a generation that no conforming final reader accepts while their consumers move forward.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Namespace-specific package ownership determines which definitions survive duplicate reconciliation.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: Uniform generation overrides a package owner's legitimate independent versioning policy.

decisions.coding_notes: Preserves the earlier freeze proposal as a superseded alternative rather than rewriting the issue's history.

decisions.title: Stamp the new generation only after both transforms complete
decisions.decision_statement: Carrier definition and instance transforms run while legacy instanceIndex enumeration remains available, relation conversion and retired-property removal follow, and one shared final step stamps dataModelRevision 2 and srsj 2 across the complete inventory.

sources.excerpt: Accepted RFC-038 pins ordering below step granularity and subsumes RFC-039's separate stamp into one final step so the corpus is never stamped while still carrying retired indexes.

alternatives: Stamp during RFC-039 before removing instanceIndex.
Delete instanceIndex before using it for RFC-039's exhaustive count assertion.
Stamp each repository whenever its local transform finishes.
decisions.accepted_cost: The migration must retain and use a soon-to-be-retired authority until all carrier assertions finish, and the final stamp becomes a cross-artifact synchronization point.
supersedes: RFC-039 Phase 2 step 8 as a separate stamping action

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Premature stamping would assert generation-2 conformance over a manifest shape generation 2 forbids.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: The order is an executable sequence with measurable count assertions rather than only an architectural ideal.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Purity of transitional state adds choreography without reducing an observable risk.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Deleting the old index too early would discard the authoritative enumeration needed to prove no legacy instances were skipped.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: The index is deleted immediately after it has discharged its one-off migration role.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: A transitional legacy authority survives beyond the cutover proof that needs it.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Per-repository stamping could expose a mixed public generation across artifacts and clients.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Repositories can prepare locally before the shared final stamp and retain separate validation evidence.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: The synchronization point creates avoidable lockstep across otherwise isolated artifacts.

decisions.coding_notes: Counts as a reasoned ordering choice, not as votes for each mechanical transform step.

decisions.title: Abort rather than partially migrate ambiguous data
decisions.decision_statement: The migration fails the whole repository with a targeted diagnostic on any input the new shape cannot represent unambiguously; it never skips, coerces, chooses a winner, or leaves a partially migrated dual-shape repository.

sources.excerpt: Accepted RFC-039 gives every schema-legal branch an explicit disposition and defines abort as failure of the entire repository, never skip, coerce, or partial migration.

alternatives: Skip records that cannot migrate.
Coerce ambiguous or malformed values into the closest new shape.
Migrate valid files and leave failures in the old carrier.
decisions.accepted_cost: One problematic value blocks migration of its whole repository and requires repair or an explicit normative disposition before the cutover can proceed.
supersedes: Best-effort migration behavior implied by incomplete earlier transform plans

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Coercion or winner selection would silently invent or discard semantic content.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: Diagnostics name the record, key, and reason so a blocked migration is actionable.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Fail-closed handling blocks useful recovery even when a reversible, explicit repair exists.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Partial migration would destroy the coherent pre-cutover state without producing a valid replacement.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: Known intentional losses have separate logged dispositions so not every non-round-trip case aborts.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Preserving exact input prevents removal of demonstrably redundant or meaningless legacy states.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Best-effort repositories would contain incompatible carriers and no singular generation contract.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Repairs are made at the owning repository or package before the shared cutover.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: One local anomaly holds all otherwise independent migration targets behind a global gate.

decisions.coding_notes: This is the failure policy; individual abort branches are mechanical derivations and do not receive separate votes.

decisions.title: Prove migration parity from pinned baselines
decisions.decision_statement: Each target records a pinned pre-migration baseline, identity sets, content hashes, counts, and validation results; acceptance requires old-to-new logical equivalence except for explicitly enumerated, logged losses whose alternatives were rejected.

sources.excerpt: Accepted RFC-038 requires per-tree baseline counts, identifier sets, hashes, and both sides of every explicitly reconciled conflict before writes begin.
Accepted RFC-039 requires full-corpus round-trip evidence and explicitly narrows equivalence only for logged valueless pairs and redundant value/entries duplication.

alternatives: Rely on green current-schema validation after migration.
Compare only aggregate file counts.
Demand byte-for-byte reversibility even for explicitly removed redundancy.
decisions.accepted_cost: The cutover must build corpus-specific audit tooling and retain evidence for intentional exceptions instead of relying on ordinary tests alone.
derived_from: RFC-039 review discovery of hidden roots and dual-written values

integrity_expression.counterfactual: A green validator can still accept skipped records, lost provenance, or a semantically changed fixture.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: The evidence is expressed as reproducible counts, hashes, and logical comparisons contributors can inspect.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: The proof measures artifacts exhaustively but misses the user-visible behavior the migration exists to preserve.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Breaking migration without before/after equivalence evidence could silently sever identity, order, history, or content.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: Explicitly justified losses permit removal of null, valueless placeholders, and redundant encodings rather than requiring false byte parity.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Parity requirements preserve accidental legacy behavior after its cost is understood and accepted.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Each repository could declare success using incompatible evidence and omit cross-artifact references.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Baselines are recorded per target and conflicts retain repository-specific owner dispositions.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: A central evidence template ignores a target's materially different storage semantics.

decisions.coding_notes: Known permitted losses are safeguards inside one parity decision, not repeated conceptual votes.

decisions.title: Repair first-party conflicts instead of deleting valid data
decisions.decision_statement: Every migrated repository is made conformant by preserving logical IDs, semantic content, relations, containers, source documents, and valid revision history, while known conflicts and missing schemas are repaired before stamping rather than ignored or resolved by deleting meaningful data.

sources.excerpt: The owner boundary says to make every migrated repository conformant, preserve meaningful content and history, and repair conflicts and schema gaps rather than delete valid data.
RFC-038 Phase 0 turns dangling IDs, invalid manifests, missing protocol and revision schemas, and duplicate ownership into hard prerequisites with explicit repairs.

alternatives: Record known fatal errors and migrate anyway.
Delete unclassifiable but valid history.
Relax the final conformance rules to admit current defects.
decisions.accepted_cost: The migration accumulates prerequisite repairs and schema work that increase scope and can block the entire release train.
supersedes: RFC-038 Revision 3 option to record #307 as a known failure

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Relaxation or deletion would make the final contract fit the implementation by erasing valid meaning or concealing contradictions.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: Repairs are concrete and bounded to observed first-party conflicts rather than abstract model expansion.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Every historical artifact is treated as meaningful even when it has no effective use or authority.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Deleting revision history, identifiers, relations, or source documents would achieve a cleaner generation by severing lineage.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: Invalid duplicate representations and obsolete carriers are removed after their valid content is reconciled.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Preservation blocks correction of legacy data whose meaning is demonstrably wrong.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Known local exceptions would make some migrated repositories fail the shared final contract.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Namespace and repository ownership determine the authoritative copy and the specific repair.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: Shared conformance forces repair of harmless local data that no consumer reads.

decisions.coding_notes: The individual Phase-0 repairs are manifestations of this policy unless they contain a separately reversible owner choice.

decisions.title: Relocate the legacy purpose document rather than adopt it
decisions.decision_statement: The unindexed legacy spec/srs-purpose-and-scope.md is moved out of sourceDocumentsPath rather than added to the authoritative source-document set; the first-party source-document membership therefore remains unchanged at four.

sources.excerpt: RFC-038 Revision 9 records the owner disposition to relocate the legacy content and not adopt it into the source-document set.
The accepted RFC's Revision 9 commit specifically records the owner disposition for Phase 0 step 2.

alternatives: Adopt the legacy document into the authoritative source-document set.
Delete the legacy content.
Leave it under sourceDocumentsPath as an unindexed contradiction.
decisions.accepted_cost: The historical document remains outside the live source-document model and requires a clearly non-authoritative destination.
derived_from: Owner assessment that the document is a legacy of early work

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Adoption would turn location accident into authoritative membership; leaving it in place would retain a contradiction.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: The content is preserved in a historical, non-authoritative location rather than erased.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Authority purity hides useful origin material from contributors.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Deletion would discard history, while adoption would preserve an invalid live classification.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: Relocation preserves the artifact while correcting its current semantic status.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Historical material survives without a maintained explanation of its relationship to the current spec.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: An unindexed file inside the reserved authoritative location would contradict the common discovery contract.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: The artifact remains available outside that location as locally maintained history.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: Reserved-location coherence disallows useful colocated context that is clearly marked non-authoritative.

decisions.coding_notes: The ratified membership disposition is distinct from the later unresolved destination/sidecar mechanics.

decisions.title: Use dataModelRevision as the generation discriminator
decisions.decision_statement: Repository and package generation is declared by monotonic dataModelRevision, with absence meaning generation 0 rather than inference from retired properties.

sources.excerpt: RFC-038 uses manifest dataModelRevision plus srsj versioning and requires old readers and final readers to fail loudly rather than infer from missing fields.
Rules R20 and R21 define generation stamps, archive version, reader rejection, and the explicit-opt-in migrator exception.

alternatives: Infer generation from the presence or absence of retired properties.
Let artifact classes invent different discriminators.
decisions.accepted_cost: Every generation-2 artifact manifest must be stamped consistently before ordinary readers accept it.
supersedes: Absence-of-instanceIndex as an implicit generation test

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Shape inference could interpret a malformed or partially migrated artifact as a valid generation.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: Diagnostics name the file and expected generation, and the structural fieldValues distinction remains simple to inspect.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Strict stamping rejects data whose generation is otherwise unambiguous and recoverable.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Runtime coercion would preserve access to generation-1 artifacts after the deliberate breaking cutover.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: An explicit opt-in migration tool may read old data and git history preserves the old runtime.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: A hard version boundary strands legitimate archives after external use begins.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Artifact-specific or heuristic discrimination would let implementations disagree about what generation they loaded.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Backends remain free to implement storage differently behind the common generation contract.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: A single artifact-generation rule prevents safe local import strategies.

decisions.coding_notes: Narrowed to generation discrimination; archive binding, runtime rejection, and migrator exception are separate atoms.

decisions.title: Expand the migrated discovery fixture into an executable predicate oracle
decisions.decision_statement: The proposed fixture migration preserves all legacy scenario identities and results while adding positive and constructed negative cases for every RFC-032 Revision-7 fieldType classification, list ordering, and the final Tier-1 disposition; it closes only in the atomic Phase-B train.

sources.excerpt: The open issue specifies the fixture migration, preservation requirements, full positive/negative classification matrix, list behavior, and atomic closure gate.
The audit finds that srs-rust declares ext:discovery but no runner executes the normative scenarios, and files srs-rust#793 as a pre-migration oracle prerequisite.

alternatives: Mechanically migrate the existing fixture without expanding predicate coverage.
Test only current first-party positive cases.
Add the conformance runner after the oracle itself has changed.
decisions.accepted_cost: The migration gains constructed cases with no current corpus use and must land a conformance runner before changing the normative fixture.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: A green migration over only existing data would not prove that exclusions or unknown formats retain their intended semantics.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: Scenario IDs, values, ordering, and legacy expected results remain contributor-readable and stable.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: The fixture becomes a model-completeness exercise disconnected from discovery behavior users need.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Either unchanged coverage would leave the new rules prose-only or wholesale replacement could redefine the legacy oracle.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: New classifications are added while all eight legacy mappings and results are preserved.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Preserving every prior scenario prevents simplifying an obsolete fixture design.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Implementations could claim ext:discovery while applying different untested classifications.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: The fixture owns only discovery consequences and explicitly leaves recursive composite search to a later RFC.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: A shared oracle expands into semantics its owning RFC deliberately left open.

decisions.coding_notes: Proposal status keeps this open task out of bias counts; it records intended acceptance, not delivered behavior.

decisions.title: Resolve the relocated charter sidecar disposition
decisions.decision_statement: It remains unresolved whether the legacy purpose document's .meta.json sidecar follows the content out of sourceDocumentsPath as RFC-038 currently says or is deleted so the relocation does not create a dangling sidecar that violates the source-document contract.

sources.excerpt: Accepted RFC-038 Revision 9 currently says to relocate the content file and its sidecar together.

The open charter-disposition issue identifies the relocated sidecar as dangling outside sourceDocumentsPath and recommends deletion, explicitly noting that this would amend accepted Phase 0 step 2 and requires owner disposition.
The cutover tracker records both the proposed governance-origin destination and the still-open sidecar choice before Phase 0 executes.

alternatives: Relocate the sidecar alongside the historical content as currently ratified.
Delete the sidecar while preserving the content in a bannered historical location.
Redefine a valid sidecar role outside sourceDocumentsPath.
decisions.accepted_cost: No alternative has been accepted; leaving it unresolved blocks an internally conformant execution of the otherwise-ratified relocation.

decisions.title: Close definition-layer gaps in the model rather than a remainder overlay
decisions.decision_statement: Metamodel v1.1.0 must express the live definition-layer surface in SRS records and emit the complete artifact; it must not depend on a hand-maintained remainder overlay for meaning the records cannot carry.
